findings.rationale: The jump host security group permits TCP 22 ingress from 0.0.0.0/0, leaving the administrative shell reachable from any internet address.
The escalation role trusts the jump role for sts:AssumeRole and carries a policy attachment that broadens its authority beyond the minimum needed for the workload.
The connectivity graph links the internet-reachable jump host to the escalation role through sts:AssumeRole, creating a direct path from network exposure to identity compromise.
The wildcard identity policy compounds with the bucket's public-read ACL, allowing an overprivileged identity to reach data that is already exposed to unauthenticated users.

findings.rationale: The identity policy grants Action and Resource as wildcards, permitting every action on every matching resource instead of the minimum set required by the workload.
